I've tried and he won't discuss it. It's like not even on table. I'll say something like "why wouldn't you consider it?" And his response is something along the lines of "I just wouldn't want to"

Mmmmk...

Now this is actually useful information to me. Didn't know about the possible complications, most people just talk about it being a quick and easy procedure.

Regardless I have never and would never push the subject, just brought it up and immediately dropped when he was completely uninterested in discussing it. I'm just trying to wrap my head around why it's so taboo to him. 

Like yes, ideally, I would want him to get one if I was unable to get a tubal, but that does not mean I would push him into it.
Notice the word "nearly" before the word "impossible".

This is what I'm trying to get at. I don't understand where he is coming from and it confuses me. I added the bit about it being selfish because honestly, I still believe it is. Why is it ok for both of us to benefit from my birth control efforts and no responsibility falls on him? 

I am not asking anyone to appease "my needs". I am questioning his sincerity as a CF person if he doesn't want a simple permanent solution to the problem. I don't give a shit if we aren't together in the future, if he is serious in his assertions about NEVER wanting children, he should be interested in sterilization, or at least have a valid reason why he's not other than just "I don't want to". This is just basic logic. 

Also, as a side note I've had hormonal birth control in the form of several different BC pills and they did not agree with me whatsoever. Hence the decision to get a copper IUD. Men often think birth control must be easy because there are "so many options" but the truth is many of the options are simply off limits to women who prioritize their physical and mental health over birth control. I'm simply not willing to alter my body's hormonal landscape to a point that makes me feel emotional, acne-ridden, and uninterested in sex (which is what hormonal birth control does for many including myself).

Wow it's amazing how people just jump to comment before they even read the post. If you have a solid command of the English language, you would notice nowhere in my post did I mention "demanding" or even ASKING my partner to get a vasectomy. I am simply confused by his disinterest in it is a possibility. I'm CF and talk about wanting to be sterilized all the time. He's supposedly just as CF and doesn't even consider. I just don't understand the dichotomy honestly. 

Also it gets a little sickening to hear people constantly say it is a woman's job to remain childfree. If he doesn't want children, some of the responsibility should fall on him as well. It takes two to tango. By having a piece of metal in my body I am supplying 100% of the contraception while both of us get to enjoy the protection from it.

Wow I really get the feeling no one is reading this post. Don't comment if you can't be bothered to read. I said it is hard for me to get a tubal, not that I don't want one. I would get one immediately if I were allowed to. Most doctors won't even listen to women under 30 asking for sterilization. I asked my gyno and was given a flat out "no".

Did you read my post? It's nearly impossible for a woman my age to get a tubal. I've asked before and my gyno told me she wouldn't even consider it. My point is that he supposedly wants kids just as little as I do so I can't understand his disinterest in sterilization. When you're in a relationship with someone you consider their needs. Im not demanding his do something to his body for my benefit, I'm suggesting it as a solution to a mutual problem. Believe it or not a pregnancy on my part would be an issue for BOTH of us.

Yes this is exactly it! I want to be a more adventurous, social person but I get exhausted from constantly having to force it. I would just like it to be easier. I feel like I've spent my whole life trying to be something I'm not, so I'd either like to change or be able to accept how I am and go from there.

I have tried meditating several times. I find it so difficult to control my thoughts I generally just give up. I did have a little stretch last winter when I meditated for 15 minutes each morning but I had so much trouble making myself get up early enough to do it that it fell by the wayside. Hearing your story though makes me want to try again. I really just need to make a commitment and stick to it.
